narrative.title: The Underfloor Pipe Ledger
narrative.scenario: A plant inspector maps a tree-shaped sprinkler network from beneath the floor: each junction's sub-pipes fan one column left and one column right, and the lowest pipe in a column covers everything above it. The report lists one junction per column, left to right — and when two junctions occupy the same column at equal depth, the one reached later in a level sweep takes the ledger slot.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child. The root sits at column 0.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array of bottom-view values, one per column, ordered left to right.

testCases.explanation: Column 0's deepest pair are 5 and 6; the later-swept 6 holds the slot.
Deeper nodes 4 and 5 cover the root's column and column 2 respectively.

hintLevels: Level 1: The mirror image of the top view — each column's deepest node wins instead of the shallowest.
Level 2: Sweep level by level and unconditionally overwrite the column's record; BFS order settles same-depth ties.
Level 3: Emit the map's keys in sorted order; no per-node depth comparison is needed because BFS visits columns in non-decreasing depth.
